name: San Antonio
tagline: River Walk Charm, Tex-Mex Heaven, and No State Income Tax
description: San Antonio is one of America's most underrated FIRE destinations, offering big-city amenities with a remarkably low cost of living and zero state income tax. The iconic River Walk, a deeply rooted Tex-Mex food culture, and centuries of Spanish colonial history give the city a character unlike anywhere else in the country. With affordable housing, warm weather, and a genuine sense of community, San Antonio rewards budget-conscious retirees with a rich and flavorful daily life.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – typical large US city with safe suburban areas
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical with hot summers and mild winters

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable studio or older 1BR in a workable area — the Medical Center or the Southtown fringe

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with affordable Tex-Mex ingredients; breakfast tacos a few times a week

healthcare.description: ACA marketplace Silver plan, subsidized if MAGI is kept under the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); assumes an early retiree (45–55) — older retirees budget more. Texas has no state backfill and did not expand Medicaid, so above the cliff this line jumps toward the full ~$925/mo sticker. Excellent military medical facilities are available if eligible.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas — a car is necessary in San Antonio (Texas insurance runs above the US average, though gas is cheap)

entertainment.description: Free River Walk strolls, the Alamo and the missions, park trails; an occasional Spurs game on a deal

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable studio or older one-bedroom near the Medical Center or on the Southtown fringe, cooking at home most nights with affordable Tex-Mex ingredients and a paid-off car to get around. The River Walk and the missions are free, and breakfast tacos cost a few dollars. Healthcare takes a meaningful share and there isn't much room for surprises, but zero state income tax helps every dollar go further — San Antonio is among the cheapest cities in the batch. The Silver premium stays low only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff.

housing.description: A decent typical 1BR in a solid neighborhood — near the Pearl or a nice area

dining.description: Regular dining at Pearl District and River Walk spots; weekend barbecue pilgrimages

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff (no Texas backfill)

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage for Hill Country drives

entertainment.description: Spurs tickets, a Museum of Art membership, live music at Gruene Hall

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in a solid neighborhood or near the Pearl, dining out several times a week at the area's restaurants and food stalls, and a reliable car for weekend drives to the Hill Country. Spurs tickets, a good health plan, and a few trips a year all fit. San Antonio's moderate costs mean this tier delivers a genuinely comfortable daily life with room to spare.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR or small home in walkable Monte Vista, Southtown, or King William

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at Mixtli, Cured, and The Granary

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear

transportation.description: A late-model SUV, premium insurance, weekend trips to Fredericksburg

entertainment.description: Premium Spurs tickets, golf club access, Symphony season tickets, spa treatments

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality home in Monte Vista or a walkable place in King William, regular dinners at Mixtli and Cured, and premium Spurs tickets. Good coverage, a late-model SUV, and regular weekend trips to Fredericksburg and the Hill Country wine region are all within budget. At this tier San Antonio feels affluent — you eat well, live in a desirable neighborhood, and have real flexibility for travel and hobbies.

housing.description: A luxury condo or upscale rental in a prime district — a Pearl high-rise or the Alamo Heights edge

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining plus occasional private-chef entertaining

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge or direct primary care

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus premium insurance and a Hill Country ranch vehicle

entertainment.description: Courtside Spurs tickets, a San Antonio Country Club membership, art collecting

domesticHelp.description: Bi-weekly cleaning, landscaping, pool service, some personal-assistant tasks

luxuryExtras.description: Hill Country ranch weekends, quarterly travel, wine-cellar curation, philanthropic giving

5M.lifestyle: A luxury condo in a Pearl high-rise or an upscale rental on the Alamo Heights edge, cleaning a couple of times a week, and a nice car. Near-daily dining at the city's best tables, concierge medical coverage, and business class for longer trips are routine, with easy weekend runs to a Hill Country cabin. San Antonio's low costs and zero state income tax make this a very comfortable, well-staffed life with margin for travel and giving.

housing.description: A top-of-market historic estate in Alamo Heights or Terrell Hills, or a Hill Country ranch compound minutes out

dining.description: Private-chef dining, catered events, and exclusive culinary experiences

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge medicine and executive wellness

transportation.description: Multiple luxury vehicles, ranch vehicles, private car service, chartered flights from SAT

entertainment.description: A private suite at the arena, major philanthropy, art collecting, international travel

domesticHelp.description: Full-time estate manager, housekeeper, personal assistant, and grounds/pool crew

luxuryExtras.description: A Hill Country ranch operation, first-class international travel, art patronage, major philanthropy

10M.lifestyle: A historic Alamo Heights estate or a Hill Country ranch compound minutes from the city, full-time domestic help, and a private chef several days a week, with concierge healthcare. Dining is anywhere without checking the bill, travel is first class, and the garage holds a vehicle or two. San Antonio's low cost base makes this budget stretch far — roughly $192k a year — with plenty left for charitable giving. Texas's zero income tax keeps every withdrawal dollar intact.
